question: When electrolysis of brine is done, a gas X is formed at the cathode, which gives a pop sound when a burning splinter is brought near it. The gas X is:
solution:
The correct answer is **H2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hydrogen's symbol is **H **and atomic number is **1**.
 
• It is the lightest element and most abundant in the universe.
 
• It is found in water **(H₂O**) and most organic compounds.
 
• It is used as a fuel in **rockets **and **clean energy systems**.
 
• It exists in **diatomic** form (H₂) under normal conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brine **can be obtained from industrial facilities, salt mining operations, or the waste stream of reverse **osmosis **(RO) **desalination plants**, and can be processed to produce useful chemicals like **sodium hydroxide** (NaOH) or **hydrochloric acid** (HCl).
 
• Due to their efficiency as **conductors **and the quantity of free electrons they have available for transfer, **carbon electrodes** are utilised in **electrolysis**.
 
• **Carbon **not only has a high melting point but is also a good conductor of **electricity**, which means that it can facilitate a variety of reactions.
 
• Salt hydroxide, hydrogen, and chlorine are produced during the electrolysis of brine.
 
• Hydrogen is a byproduct regularly burned with chlorine in the traditional chlor-alkali business to create hydrochloric acid.​
